problems.title: Turn a logarithmic exponent into a square
problems.question: Find the sum of the real roots of $x^{\log_4x}=4$.
problems.idea: Write x as a power of 4.
steps: The logarithm requires x>0. Put t=log₄x.
Then 4^(t²)=4, so t²=1 and t=1 or -1.
The roots are x=4 and x=1/4; their sum is 17/4.

problems.title: Subtract the base diagonals from space diagonals
problems.question: A right prism has a rhombus base of side 4.5 and space diagonals 8 and 5. Find its height.
problems.idea: Both space diagonals contain the same vertical contribution.
formulas: For a rhombus, d₁²+d₂²=4s²; in a right prism Dᵢ²=dᵢ²+h².
steps: Add the two space-diagonal equations: 8²+5²=4(4.5)²+2h².
Thus 89=81+2h² and h²=4.
The positive height is h=2.

problems.title: Chain logarithms
problems.question: Evaluate $\log_3 6\cdot\log_6 27$.
problems.idea: The middle logarithm bases cancel under change of base.
steps: The product is log₃27.
Since 27=3³, this equals 3.

problems.title: Volume of a regular hexagonal prism
problems.question: The greatest diagonal section of a regular hexagonal prism has area 4. Opposite lateral faces are 2 apart. Find the volume.
problems.idea: Express both given measurements in terms of the hexagon side and prism height.
formulas: A regular hexagon of side s has longest diagonal 2s, opposite-side distance √3s and area 3√3s²/2; V=base area·h.
steps: The diagonal section gives 2sh=4.
The face separation gives √3s=2.

problems.title: Remember negative inputs allowed by even powers
problems.question: Find the sum of the roots of $[\lg(100/x^4)]^2+[\lg(10000x^2)]^2=40$.
problems.idea: Both logarithms depend on |x|.
steps: The domain is all x≠0, including negative x.
Thus |x|=10 or 1/10, giving x=±10,±1/10.
Opposite roots cancel, so their sum is 0.

problems.title: A tetrahedron with equal connecting edges
problems.question: Two opposite edges of a tetrahedron have lengths 16 and 18. Its other four edges are 17. Find the volume.
problems.idea: The opposite edges are perpendicular, with their midpoints separated perpendicularly to both.
formulas: V=abH/6 for perpendicular opposite edges of lengths a,b separated by H; Pythagoras.
steps: Place the first edge endpoints at (±8,0,0). Equal distances force the second edge into the plane x=0.
Its midpoint may be (0,H,0) and its endpoints (0,H,±9). Equal connecting edges also make the two edge directions perpendicular.
The length 17 gives 8²+9²+H²=17², so H=12.

problems.title: Separate the three lateral faces
problems.question: A pyramid has an equilateral base of side a. One lateral face is equilateral and perpendicular to the base. Find the lateral surface area.
problems.idea: Use coordinates to calculate the two equal remaining face areas.
formulas: Triangle area=|u×v|/2; an equilateral triangle has area √3a²/4.
steps: Face SAB has area √3a²/4. For face SAC, vectors AC=(a/2,√3a/2,0) and AS=(a/2,0,√3a/2) have squared cross-product length 15a⁴/16.
Thus each of SAC,SBC has area √15a²/8.
Add the three areas.

problems.title: A negative logarithm fixes the denominator sign
problems.question: Solve $\dfrac{\log_{1/2}(x^2+3)}{4x^2-16x}>0$.
problems.idea: The numerator is always negative.
formulas: If 0<b<1 and u>1, then log_b u<0.
steps: Since x²+3≥3>1, the logarithm is strictly negative.
A positive quotient therefore needs 4x(x-4)<0.
This holds exactly for 0<x<4; the excluded endpoints make the denominator zero.

problems.title: Distance to a cone generator
problems.question: A cone has base radius 15. The base centre is distance 12 from a generator line. Find the height.
problems.idea: In the axial right triangle, this distance is the altitude to the hypotenuse.
steps: Thus h²=400 and h=20.

problems.title: Reciprocal logarithms with domain checks
problems.question: Solve $\log_{3x+7}(2x+3)^2+\log_{2x+3}[(3x+7)(2x+3)]=4$.
problems.idea: Let one logarithm be t and express the other using 1/t.
steps: The bases require x>-3/2 and x≠-1; then A=3x+7>1 and B=2x+3>0, B≠1.
The equation becomes 2t+1+1/t=4, hence (2t-1)(t-1)=0.
If t=1, B=A gives x=-4, outside the domain. If t=1/2, B²=A gives 4x²+9x+2=0.
These roots are -1/4 and -2. Only -1/4 satisfies the original domain.

problems.title: A rational inequality in 2 to the x
problems.question: Solve $1/(2^x-1)>1/(1-2^{x-1})$.
problems.idea: Substitute t=2ˣ and make a sign chart.
steps: Exclude t=1,2. The critical values are 1,4/3,2.
The expression is positive on (1,4/3) and (2,∞), and negative on the other positive intervals.
Since 2ˣ increases, these intervals give 0<x<log₂(4/3) or x>1.

problems.title: A square vertical section of a cylinder
problems.question: A cylinder has height 2 and base radius √5. A plane perpendicular to its base cuts a square. Find the distance from the cylinder axis to the plane.
problems.idea: The square’s horizontal side is a chord of length equal to the cylinder height.
formulas: For a chord of length c at distance d from a circle centre, d²+(c/2)²=r².
steps: The vertical square side is 2, so its horizontal chord also has length 2.
Thus d²+1²=5.
The nonnegative distance is d=2.

problems.title: An interval absent from the choices
problems.question: Solve $\log_{1.3}(0.67)\,\log_{1/3}(x-3)<0$.
problems.idea: Check the sign of the constant logarithm first.
formulas: For b>1, log_b u<0 when 0<u<1; for 0<b<1, log_b u>0 when 0<u<1.
steps: Since 0.67<1 and 1.3>1, the first factor is negative.
The second factor must therefore be positive, giving 0<x-3<1.
Thus 3<x<4. None of the printed numerical choices 2,1,5,0,√5,3 is in this interval.
problems.answer: All real x in (3,4); none of the listed choices.
problems.note: The printed choices do not include any valid solution.

problems.title: A variable logarithm base
problems.question: Solve $\log_{x^2+1}(x^2+3x)>1$.
problems.idea: The valid base is greater than 1.
formulas: For b>1, log_b u>1 iff u>b.
steps: The base is valid for x≠0.
The inequality becomes x²+3x>x²+1, giving x>1/3.
These x also make both the base valid and the argument positive.

problems.title: Area of an off-axis cone section
problems.question: A cone has height 6 and base radius 3. A vertex section cuts a base chord subtending 90°. Find the section area.
problems.idea: Use the chord midpoint to find the altitude within the section.
formulas: c=2r sin45°; centre-to-chord distance d=r cos45°; section altitude=√(h²+d²); area=c·altitude/2.
steps: The chord is 3√2 and its distance from the base centre is 3/√2.
The section altitude is √(36+9/2)=9/√2.

problems.title: Reverse the inequality for a small positive base
problems.question: Solve $(4-2\sqrt3)^{(1-5x)/(x+2)}\ge\sqrt[3]{(4+2\sqrt3)/4}$.
problems.idea: Both sides can use the same base less than 1.
steps: The right side is A^(-1/3). The decreasing exponential reverses the comparison of exponents.
The pole is -2 and the zero is 5/14. The quotient is nonpositive for x<-2 or x≥5/14.

problems.title: Volume from an inclined lateral edge
problems.question: A regular hexagonal pyramid has lateral edge 4 inclined 60° to the base. Find its volume.
problems.idea: The edge’s projection is the hexagon circumradius, equal to its side.
steps: The height is 2√3 and the hexagon side is 2.
The base area is 6√3.

problems.title: Sphere through the cube vertices
problems.question: Find the radius of a sphere circumscribed around a cube of edge 2.
problems.idea: The space diagonal is a sphere diameter.
steps: The space diagonal is 2√3.
Half of it is √3.

problems.title: Recover lateral area from diagonal sections
problems.question: A right prism with rhombus base has diagonal-section areas 20 and 15. Find its lateral area.
problems.idea: The squared base diagonals add to four side-length squares.
steps: The section areas are d₁h=20 and d₂h=15.
Thus (2sh)²=20²+15²=625, so 2sh=25.
The lateral area is 4sh=50.

problems.title: Express a logarithm using lg2
problems.question: Given $\lg2=a$, express $\log_5 10$.
problems.idea: Use change of base.
steps: lg10=1 and lg5=1-a.
Therefore log₅10=1/(1-a).

problems.title: A quadratic always has two valid logarithmic roots
problems.question: For which real a does $\lg(x^2+ax)=2$ have two distinct real roots?
problems.idea: The logarithmic equation fixes its argument at 100.
steps: The equation is x²+ax-100=0.
Its discriminant a²+400 is strictly positive for every real a.
Each resulting root makes the original argument exactly 100, so both are valid.

problems.title: Simplify powers before multiplying
problems.question: Evaluate $8^{(2/3)\log_2\sqrt{3+\sqrt2}}\,27^{(1/3)\log_3(3-\sqrt2)}$.
problems.idea: Write 8=2³ and 27=3³.
steps: The first factor is 2^[2log₂√(3+√2)]=3+√2.
The second is 3^[log₃(3-√2)]=3-√2.
Their product is 9-2=7.

problems.title: An equation true throughout its domain
problems.question: Solve $(x-1)^{\log_4(2x)}=(2x)^{\log_4(x-1)}$.
problems.idea: Use the symmetry of logarithmic exponents.
formulas: $a^{\log_c b}=b^{\log_c a}$ for a,b>0 and c>0,c≠1.
steps: The two logarithms require x-1>0 and 2x>0, so x>1.
On that domain both sides equal 4^[(log₄(x-1))(log₄(2x))].
Thus every x>1 is a solution.

problems.title: A logarithm identity cannot equal another integer
problems.question: How many roots does $\log_x(x^2)=k$ have if k is an integer different from 2?
problems.idea: First impose the restrictions on a logarithm base.
steps: The admissible bases are x>0 with x≠1.
For every such base, x² is exactly its second power, so the logarithm is 2.
It cannot equal the given k≠2.

problems.title: Range of an exponential with a cosine quadratic
problems.question: Find the range of $y=4^{\cos^2x+\cos x}$.
problems.idea: Find the exponent’s full range before applying the increasing exponential.
steps: The minimum exponent is -1/4 at t=-1/2.
The maximum is 2 at t=1. The exponent attains every intermediate value.
Since base 4>1, the range is [4^(-1/4),4²].
